intro.data: Chaining boxed steps tends to nest boxes inside boxes — a Maybe holding a Maybe. The monad's other move is 'join': collapse a double box into a single one, KEEPING what's there. The tray holds two machines — one merges it faithfully, one crushes it to nothing. Bring the faithful join onto the board and wire it, leaving the impostor in the tray.
intro.alchemy: Chaining sealed steps tends to nest vials inside vials. The monad's other move is to Decant: pour a vial-of-a-vial into one vial, KEEPING the contents. The tray holds two apparatus — one decants faithfully, one tips it all out. Bring the faithful decant onto the board and wire it, leaving the impostor in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: Chaining bound steps tends to nest charms inside charms. The monad's other move is to Merge: fold a charm-of-a-charm into one, KEEPING the essence. The tray holds two runes — one merges faithfully, one snuffs it out. Bring the faithful merge onto the board and wire it, leaving the impostor in the tray.
intro.abstract: Just x means the value x is present; Nothing means absent; join (μ : T(T(A)) → T(A)) flattens a box-in-a-box, keeping the value. From the tray bring μ and wire T(T(A)) to T(A); the impostor has the same type but collapses Just (Just 3) to Nothing, so leave it behind.

goal.data: Bring the right machine from the tray and flatten the double box, keeping the user inside.

goal.abstract: Bring μ from the tray and wire T(T(A)) to T(A), sending Just (Just 3) ↦ Just 3.

afterSuccess.data: 'join' collapsed a box-in-a-box into a single box, keeping the user. That flattening is what makes chaining possible: do a step that returns a box, and join the nesting away. The 'Crush' look-alike had the right type but discarded the contents.
afterSuccess.alchemy: 'Decant' poured the vial-of-vial into one, keeping the herb — the flattening that makes chaining possible. 'Tip Out' had the right type but discarded the contents.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: 'Merge' folded the charm-of-charm into one, keeping the rune — the flattening that makes chaining possible. 'Snuff' had the right type but lost the essence.
afterSuccess.abstract: μ : T(T(A)) → T(A) flattens the nesting, preserving content. With η it is the structure of a monad; bind g = μ ∘ T(g).

reveal.summary: join (μ : T(T(A)) → T(A)) flattens a box-inside-a-box into one box. It's what lets you chain a step that returns a box and not drown in nesting — bind g = join ∘ map(g).
